notes.summary: Statistical inference draws conclusions about a population from a sample: estimating parameters (point and interval) and testing hypotheses with z, t, χ² and F tests. JSO asks definitions, confidence intervals, test statistics and degrees of freedom.

concepts.title: Estimation
concepts.body:
• A good estimator is unbiased, consistent, efficient and sufficient.
  • Sample mean is unbiased for μ. s² = Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1) is unbiased for σ².
  • Confidence interval for μ (σ known): x̄ ± z × σ/√n. z = 1.645 (90%), 1.96 (95%), 2.576 (99%).

concepts.title: Hypothesis testing
concepts.body:
• H0 (null) vs H1 (alternative).
  • Type I error: reject H0 when it is true; probability α = level of significance.
  • Type II error: accept H0 when it is false; probability β. Power = 1 − β.
  • p-value < α ⇒ reject H0.

varieties.name: Errors and properties
varieties.how: Type I = rejecting a true H₀ (α); Type II = accepting a false H₀ (β).

example.q: A court convicts an innocent person (H₀: innocent). Which error?

varieties.name: Confidence intervals
varieties.how: x̄ ± z × SE; choose z from the confidence level.

example.q: x̄ = 80, σ = 12, n = 36. Find the 95% CI.

varieties.name: Test statistics and df
varieties.how: z = (x̄ − μ₀)/(σ/√n); look up the df rule for t, χ² and F.

example.q: Degrees of freedom of a one-sample t-test with n = 15?

tips: A wider confidence interval means more confidence but less precision.
α and β move in opposite directions for a fixed n; only a larger n reduces both.
traps: "Accepting H₀" does not prove it true; it only means there is not enough evidence against it.
Unbiased sample variance divides by n − 1, not n.
χ² df for a contingency table is (r − 1)(c − 1), not rc − 1.

questions.q: A Type I error is committed when:
options: H<sub>0</sub> is accepted when it is false
H<sub>0</sub> is rejected when it is true
H<sub>1</sub> is rejected when it is false
questions.solution: Type I error = rejecting a true null hypothesis. Its probability is α, the level of significance.

questions.q: For a 95% confidence interval using the normal distribution, the critical value z is:
questions.solution: Two-tailed 95%: 2.5% in each tail, so z = 1.96. (1.645 is for 90%, 2.576 for 99%.)
